issues.title: Phase 0 — Skeleton
issues.body:
**Status.** Delivered through PR #1.

**Work.** Go module `github.com/djm56/cairn-memory`, Go 1.25. `cmd/cairn` with the sub-command frame and `cairn version`. Makefile (`build`, `test`, `vet`, `fmt`, `run`). CI on pull requests: `go vet`, `go test -race`, `gofmt` check. MIT licence (as bishop-memory). `CONTRIBUTING.md` with the rules in §6. `.gitignore` for `bin/`, `dist/`, `*.db`.

**Exit check.** `make test` passes in CI on an empty suite; `bin/cairn version` prints a version from `git describe`.

issues.title: Phase 1 — Contract
issues.body:
**Status.** Done. The exit check passed with the operator's approval of CONTRACT.md §9 items 1–11 on 2026-10-28; item 12 is deferred to phase 8 (#41).

**Work.** `internal/core`: the `Service` interface, the request and result types for every tool in DESIGN.md §4, and the error kinds (not found, refused by policy, invalid, operator only). `docs/CONTRACT.md`: each tool's inputs, outputs, errors and an example. `internal/conformance`: a test suite that takes any `Service` and checks the behaviour, including: a whole task (start with a brief and plan, step through it, log events, record a review, add a learning, be refused at close with the missing items listed, close); inserting a step between two others without renumbering; refusing every write without a project; refusing every operator-only change through the agent interface; events are append-only and timestamps are the server's; `task_current` returns the one active task, and nothing when none is. The suite cannot pass yet; it runs against a stub that fails every call.

**Exit check.** `CONTRACT.md` covers every tool in DESIGN.md §4. The conformance suite compiles and reports every case as failing against the stub. Review of the contract by the operator before phase 2 starts.

issues.title: Phase 2 — Core and local store
issues.body:
**Work.** `internal/store`: schema v1 (DESIGN.md §3) as numbered migrations, WAL mode, busy timeout, FTS5 index and its triggers. Typed query functions for every table. `internal/core`: the `Service` implementation over the store, holding every rule: status transitions, the close policy, step positions, task-id allocation in one transaction, operator-only changes. `internal/identity`: project resolution from `CAIRN_PROJECT` and `.cairn.toml` (DESIGN.md §2.1).

**Exit check.** The conformance suite passes against the local `Service`. Two processes writing the same database at once allocate distinct task ids (a test). `go test -race` is clean.

**Guided by.** bishop-memory, for reference: `internal/store/sqlite.go` and `migrate.go`, the FTS setup from `db/schema.sql`, and the allocator's daily sequence from `internal/api/allocate.go`.

issues.title: Decide whether M1 moves internal/client and a serve skeleton in, or tests against an in-process test server
issues.body:
**Question.** M1's exit check runs against `cairn serve`, which M2 builds. Does M1 move `internal/client` and a serve skeleton into M1, or does it test against an in-process test server?

**Answer (2026-10-30, option B: test against an in-process test server, D19).** M1 tests against an in-process `httptest` server. M1 adds no network listener to the shipped binary and no `cairn serve`; its tests bind an `httptest` server to loopback (D19). The live run against `cairn serve` on another machine is M2's exit check (#19).

**Source.** [docs/PLAN.md §10](https://github.com/djm56/cairn-memory/blob/main/docs/PLAN.md#10-open-questions).

issues.title: Tracking: internal/api, the HTTP handlers over core
issues.body:
**Work.** `internal/api`: the HTTP handlers over `core`, in the form DESIGN §5.4 sets out. M1 builds them as handlers only. The shipped binary has no network listener (D19); the listener is `cairn serve`, which is M2. This issue tracks the package after M1. Its open follow-ups are:

- the wire-form decisions, #109 (M2);
- the M1 header caller and its tripwire, #110 (M2);
- the failure hook that `cairn serve` must pass, #112 (M2).

**Exit.** Closed when `cairn serve` mounts these handlers in M2 and the follow-ups above are closed.

Source: [docs/PLAN.md §3, M1](https://github.com/djm56/cairn-memory/blob/main/docs/PLAN.md#milestone-table)

M1 tests it against an in-process `httptest` server bound to loopback (D19). M2 runs it against `cairn serve`, and the live Claude Code run is M2's exit check (#19). This issue tracks the package after M1. Its open follow-ups are:

- the wire-form decisions that the client encodes, #109 (M2);
- the live run against `cairn serve`, #19 (M2).

**Exit.** Closed when M2 runs the client against `cairn serve` and the follow-ups above are closed.

issues.title: M2 Server
issues.body:
**Work.** `cairn serve`: the network listener over the `internal/api` handlers built in M1, TLS by files or behind a proxy, loopback default, body caps, `/healthz`. Keys with `agent`, `operator` and `viewer` scopes (D13). `cairn key add/list/revoke`. `cairn backup <path>` using SQLite online backup. A systemd unit in `docs/`. The directive cap (12 per call, ranked, D16) and `review_by` on directives.

**Exit check.** Conformance suite passes over HTTP; agent key refused on operator routes; viewer key refused on every write (tests); M1 flow works with `server` set; the live Claude Code run of a small task against `cairn serve` on another machine (#19), and `cairn export task` prints it.

**Guided by.** bishop-memory, for reference: `internal/auth/keys.go`, `internal/middleware`, `internal/config`, the TLS and key handling in `cmd/memoryd`, and the network tests (`internal/api/network_test.go`).

issues.title: M3 Web UI + dashboard
issues.body:
**Work.** Pages embedded in the binary, served by `cairn serve`: **Tasks**: a list across projects; one task's page with its brief, steps, journal, reviews and close record. **Learnings**: proposed findings with accept, reject and supersede, each with a note. **Directives**: ratify, scope, `review_by`, retire. **Projects**: settings, including the close policy and parallel tasks. **Dashboard**: running now, waiting on you, quality (30 days), improving (by month), and the active directive count and oldest age.

**Exit check.** A lead sees a proposed finding, accepts it, ratifies a directive, and `task_current` returns it next session; a viewer key sees every page and gets 403 on every action.

**Guided by.** bishop-memory, for reference: the mission HUD (Tasks page) and the triage review page (Learnings page).

issues.title: M6 Import
issues.body:
**Work.** `cairn import bishop-memory --db <path> [--dry-run]`. Reads the bishop-memory SQLite file directly; never reads harness Markdown. The mapping is in PLAN §5.1, with the reviewer verdicts carried as `review` events. Idempotent: running it twice changes nothing the second time. Reports counts for each table, read and written, and every row it could not map.

**Exit check.** A dry run against a copy of the live bishop-memory database maps every mission, step, event, finding, directive, criterion, lesson, mistake, deliverable and grade, or names each one it skipped and why. Counts are checked against the source. The operator reviews the result in the web UI.

issues.title: Later: scheduled review loop
issues.body:
**Work.** Build triage and grading fresh (DESIGN.md §7), guided by bishop-memory: categories, classification, groups, recommendations, directive proposals, grades, runs; the MCP review profile; the agent definitions and skills, rewritten without Bishop names; an engine-neutral runner (`cairn review run classify|process|grade`) that starts the chosen client headless. A scheduling guide for launchd and systemd.

**Exit check.** A scheduled run classifies new findings and grades closed tasks, and the operator accepts the recommendations on the review page. Then the bishop-memory nightly runs are switched off (PLAN §5.3).

**Guided by.** bishop-memory, for reference: the triage and grade routes in `internal/api/triage.go` and `grades.go`, `internal/store/triage_runs.go` and `mission_grades.go`, `scripts/triage-run.sh`, the three agents and two skills under `.claude/`, and their tests.
